answer: Verification engine binds each identity to 64 gigabytes of dedicated RAM via latency challenges. Verifier streams sequential pointer addresses requiring 15-nanosecond memory-bus response windows. Random memory hops wander across uncompressed address space, where cache misses forge deterministic timing proofs. Any delay ripple exceeding 20 nanoseconds drops session and slashes registration stake. Simulating 1,000 parallel identities requires 64 terabytes of physical DRAM costing $28,000 monthly, preventing virtualized multiplexing.
